paragraphs: Visit type: chronic lung disease clinic, six-month review. Spirometry booked before the visit.

68-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease reports his usual morning cough and breathlessness walking uphill. No increase in sputum, no fever and no steroid courses since the last visit.
Smoked 40 pack-years, quit eight years ago. Medications: tiotropium inhaler daily, salbutamol as needed. Vaccinations up to date.
Exam: oxygen saturation 94 percent at rest, scattered expiratory wheeze, no use of accessory muscles. Spirometry: post-bronchodilator FEV1 to FVC ratio 0.58, FEV1 62 percent of predicted.
Assessment: COPD, stable, no exacerbation. Plan: continue tiotropium, review inhaler technique, pulmonary rehabilitation referral.
query: chronic obstructive pulmonary disease stable no exacerbation

selection.rationale: COPD is documented as stable with no exacerbation, and emphysema or chronic bronchitis is not named.

validation.reason: No acute exacerbation is documented, so J44.1 does not apply. J44.9 is supported.

paragraphs: Visit type: cardiology clinic. Patient accompanied by his daughter.
72-year-old man seen after his family doctor found an irregular pulse. He has felt occasional fluttering and tiredness for a few weeks. No fainting, chest pain or stroke symptoms.
Past history: hypertension. Medications: amlodipine 5 mg. No bleeding history. Alcohol rarely.

Findings: heart rate 96, irregularly irregular. Electrocardiogram shows atrial fibrillation with a ventricular rate of 98. Echocardiogram shows normal left ventricular function. Thyroid function normal.
Assessment: atrial fibrillation, type not yet determined. Plan: start apixaban 5 mg twice daily, add metoprolol for rate control, 24-hour monitor to characterise the pattern.

treated.treatment: apixaban 5 mg twice daily and metoprolol

first_selection.rationale: Fluttering that comes and goes suggests paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

first_validation_reason: The assessment says the type of atrial fibrillation is not yet determined, and monitoring is planned to characterise it. Paroxysmal is not documented.

selection.rationale: Atrial fibrillation is confirmed on the electrocardiogram, and the clinician has not yet classified its type.

validation.reason: Unspecified atrial fibrillation matches an assessment with no documented type.

paragraphs: Visit type: new patient headache consultation. Headache diary brought to the visit.

33-year-old woman with recurrent one-sided throbbing headaches, two to three per month, lasting up to a day. Light and noise make them worse and she sometimes feels nauseated. No weakness, vision loss or speech change.
Family history of migraine in her mother. Medications: ibuprofen with partial relief. Uses an oral contraceptive. No known allergies.
Neurological exam normal, fundi normal, blood pressure 114/72. No red flag features. The note does not describe visual aura.
Assessment: migraine, not intractable, no status migrainosus. Plan: start sumatriptan for attacks, keep a diary, discuss preventive options if frequency rises.
query: migraine unspecified not intractable without status migrainosus

selection.rationale: Migraine is documented without a stated aura status, and it is not intractable with no status migrainosus.

validation.reason: The note neither states with aura nor without aura. G43.909 is the supported unspecified code.

paragraphs: Visit type: thyroid follow-up. Laboratory results printed for the patient.
46-year-old woman with fatigue, cold intolerance and weight gain of 4 kg over six months. She reports constipation and dry skin. No neck swelling or palpitations.
Medications: none before this visit. Family history of thyroid disease in her sister. Periods regular.
Results: TSH 14.8 mIU/L, free T4 low at 0.6 ng/dL. Heart rate 58, dry skin, delayed ankle reflex relaxation. Thyroid not enlarged.
Assessment: hypothyroidism. Plan: start levothyroxine 75 micrograms daily, repeat TSH in six weeks.
query: hypothyroidism unspecified low free T4 raised TSH

selection.rationale: Hypothyroidism is confirmed by raised TSH and low free T4, with no cause such as thyroiditis or surgery documented.

validation.reason: No autoimmune, iodine-related or postprocedural cause is stated, so E03.9 applies.

paragraphs: Visit type: same-day appointment, student health service. Appointment lasted fifteen minutes.
22-year-old woman with a sore throat for three days, pain on swallowing and a low-grade fever. No cough, runny nose or rash. No known sick contacts.
No chronic conditions. No regular medications. No allergies.
Exam: temperature 37.9 C, mildly red throat, no tonsillar exudate, tender anterior neck nodes. Rapid streptococcal test negative.
Assessment: acute pharyngitis. Plan: rest, fluids, paracetamol and throat lozenges, return if not improving in five days.
query: acute pharyngitis sore throat negative streptococcal test

selection.rationale: The assessment is acute pharyngitis, and the streptococcal test is negative so the streptococcal code does not apply.

validation.reason: Acute pharyngitis without a documented organism maps to J02.9.

paragraphs: Visit type: urology clinic review after an emergency visit. Imaging disc brought by the patient.
39-year-old man had sudden severe left flank pain with blood in the urine two days ago, now settled. No fever, vomiting or difficulty passing urine.
No previous kidney stones. Medications: ibuprofen. Drinks little water at work.
Imaging: CT shows a 6 mm stone in the left renal pelvis with no hydronephrosis and no ureteral stone. Urinalysis shows red cells, no infection. Creatinine normal.
Assessment: calculus of the left kidney, not obstructing. Plan: hydration, tamsulosin, strain urine, repeat ultrasound in four weeks.
query: calculus of kidney renal pelvis stone no obstruction

selection.rationale: The stone sits in the renal pelvis, with no ureteral stone and no hydronephrosis, so calculus of kidney applies.

validation.reason: Imaging excludes ureteral stone and obstruction, which rules out N20.1 and N13.2.

paragraphs: Visit type: surgical outpatient consultation. Referral letter and ultrasound report attached.
53-year-old woman with episodes of right upper abdominal pain after fatty meals for four months, lasting about an hour. No fever, jaundice or persistent pain.
Medications: omeprazole as needed. Two pregnancies. Weight stable.
Imaging: ultrasound shows multiple gallstones, thin gallbladder wall, no pericholecystic fluid, common bile duct 4 mm. Liver tests normal. No signs of cholecystitis.
Assessment: gallstones without cholecystitis or obstruction. Plan: schedule elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy, low-fat diet until surgery.
query: calculus of gallbladder without cholecystitis without obstruction

selection.rationale: Ultrasound shows gallstones with a normal gallbladder wall and no cholecystitis or duct obstruction.

validation.reason: The note explicitly excludes cholecystitis and obstruction. K80.20 matches.

paragraphs: Visit type: follow-up appointment, outpatient mental health. Questionnaires collected beforehand.
29-year-old man with excessive worry about work, health and money on most days for over a year. He reports restlessness, muscle tension and trouble falling asleep. The worry is hard to control.
No panic attacks, no specific phobia, no substance misuse. Medications: none. Caffeine two to three cups a day.
Mental status: anxious but cooperative, no psychotic features, no suicidal ideation. GAD-7 score 16. Physical exam and thyroid tests normal.
Impression: generalized anxiety disorder. Plan: start escitalopram 10 mg, cognitive behavioral therapy referral, reduce caffeine.

treated.treatment: escitalopram 10 mg and cognitive behavioral therapy

first_selection.rationale: The patient reports anxiety symptoms, so anxiety disorder, unspecified is a safe match.

first_validation_reason: The impression names generalized anxiety disorder specifically, which has its own code. Unspecified anxiety disorder loses that detail.

selection.rationale: The impression states generalized anxiety disorder, supported by more than a year of uncontrolled worry and a GAD-7 of 16.

validation.reason: A specific diagnosis is documented, so F41.1 is correct.

paragraphs: Triage: stroke code activated on arrival, last known well 40 minutes before arrival. Family at bedside.
69-year-old woman with sudden right arm weakness and slurred speech noticed at breakfast. No headache or trauma. Symptoms have persisted for over an hour.
Past history: hypertension and atrial fibrillation, not on anticoagulation. Medications: amlodipine. No prior stroke.

Findings: right arm drift with reduced power, mild dysarthria, NIHSS score 5. Non-contrast head CT shows no hemorrhage. MRI diffusion sequence shows an acute infarct in the left hemisphere. Vessel imaging pending.
Impression: acute ischemic stroke, cause under investigation. Plan: admit to the stroke unit, antiplatelet therapy, swallow screen, start workup for the source.

treated.treatment: antiplatelet therapy on the stroke unit

query: cerebral infarction acute ischemic stroke cause unspecified

selection.rationale: MRI confirms an acute infarct, and the mechanism is still under investigation, so cerebral infarction, unspecified applies.

validation.reason: Infarct is confirmed and no artery or mechanism is documented. I63.9 is supported.

paragraphs: Visit type: weight management discussion. Patient filled in the lifestyle questionnaire.
44-year-old man concerned about steady weight gain over ten years. He has tried several diets without lasting effect. No joint pain, breathlessness or snoring.
Medications: none. Sedentary job. Eats out several times a week. No family history of diabetes.
Exam: weight 112 kg, waist circumference 114 cm, blood pressure 130/84. Body mass index is not calculated in the note. Fasting glucose and lipids normal.
Assessment: obesity. Plan: dietitian referral, structured exercise program, review weight in three months.

selection.rationale: A weight of 112 kg with a waist of 114 cm indicates severe obesity from excess calories.

validation.reason: The measurements are consistent with a high degree of obesity, so E66.01 is accepted.
